concepts.why: The patient's skin biopsy findings of dense granulomatous infiltrate and positive CD68 immunohistochemical results are consistent with Niemann-Pick disease.
The patient's presentation of numerous asymptomatic reddish-brownish papules, nodules, and plaques over his whole body is consistent with Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
The patient's 7-year medical history of polydipsia and polyuria and diagnosis of central diabetes insipidus support this concept.
The patient's diagnosis of hypothyroidism supports this concept.
The patient's growth retardation is consistent with growth hormone deficiency.
The patient's skin biopsy findings and positive CD68 immunohistochemical results are consistent with Erdheim-Chester disease.
The patient's presentation of numerous asymptomatic reddish-brownish papules, nodules, and plaques over his whole body is consistent with sarcoidosis.
The patient's skin biopsy findings of dense granulomatous infiltrate and positive CD68 immunohistochemical results are consistent with histiocytosis.
The patient's diagnosis of central diabetes insipidus and hypothyroidism support this concept.
The patient's growth retardation is consistent with congenital disorder of glycosylation.

rationales.F01: Reddish-brown papules and plaques are more typical of histiocytosis and Erdheim-Chester disease.
rationales.F03: Polydipsia and polyuria are characteristic of diabetes insipidus.
rationales.F04: Central diabetes insipidus is a strong indicator of the disease.
rationales.F06: Hypothyroidism can be associated with autoimmune polyendocrinopathy.
rationales.F08: Dense granulomatous infiltrate is more typical of Erdheim-Chester disease and histiocytosis.
rationales.F09: Immunohistochemical results help to rule out Langerhans cell histiocytosis and support Erdheim-Chester disease and histiocytosis.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's skin biopsy findings of dense granulomatous infiltrate in the upper dermis, negative for CD1a and S-100, and positive for CD68, along with the presence of numerous asymptomatic reddish-brownish papules, nodules, and plaques over the whole body, are more consistent with Multifocal Erdheim-Chester disease.
